To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the random mutagenesis was successfully used for the generation of variant forms of C23O from Planococcus strain S5 with improved activity towards different catecholic substrates and (2) the introduced mutations in C23O structure are localized in different regions of the protein structure, but the most significant changes are located in the vicinity of C23O active site and at its surface.

we have identified the amino acid residues that are crucial for substrate recognition and binding of C23O from Planococcus S5 and that we have engineered C23O to have higher activity towards chlorinated catechols.
random mutagenesis of the c23o gene encoding catechol-2,3-dioxigenase from Planococcussp. strain S5 resulted in a mutant protein with improved activity towards 4-chlorocatechol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the new biocatalyst for bioremediations of the environmental pollutants.
the possibility of improving the enzyme properties by directed evolution and rational design.
the identification of new enzyme variants with improved properties for bioremediations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzyme activity is not only affected by the mutations located in the vicinity of active site but also by the changes located on the enzyme surface.
the C23OC61 variant is more suitable for the degradation of para-substituted compounds, whereas the mutant C23OB58 is more suitable for degradation of 4-chloro-2-hydroxybenzoic acid.
random mutagenesis is an efficient tool for engineering C23O enzyme for bioremedial purposes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal domain is a crucial factor for enzyme activity and stability.

the random mutagenesis of the C23O gene is a powerful tool to generate variants with altered properties and that the analysis of the enzyme structure based on the putatively modeled 3D structure is a useful tool to predict the effects of introduced mutations on C23O properties and to identify the key amino acid residues for enzyme activity.
the random mutagenesis approach is an efficient way to generate variant C23O enzymes with improved activity against different catechols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C23O from Planococcus S5 is a good candidate for further engineering to improve its activity towards chlorinated substrates.
the C-terminal region of C23O is crucial for enzyme activity.
it is possible to engineer catechol 3,4-dioxygenase to have a higher activity towards 4-chloro- and 4-nitrocatechols, which are the most toxic and refractory compounds in industrial wastewaters.
